## Refactor RBAC to a role inheritance graph

The per-role `if/elif` in `can()` has become unwieldy and error-prone: every new action means editing several branches, and it is hard to see what a role can actually do. This refactor expresses authorization as (1) the permissions each role *introduces* and (2) a role inheritance graph, and computes the effective permission set as the transitive closure.

Behaviour is unchanged — the effective permissions for every existing role are the same as before. An import-time self-check guards against dangling parent references, cycles, and typo'd permission strings. A new `AccessPolicy` caches closures for hot paths.

### Tests
Existing authorization tests pass unchanged (admin superuser, manager billing, editor publish, author write, viewer read-only, api_client read-only, guest content-only, plus the negative cases).
